$comment: ONE number, read by THREE gates now, and that is the whole point of the file.
check-plan-housekeeping.sh reports a plan older than delete_days.
check_plan_boxes.py's A5 REFUSES to delete a plan that still carries open
boxes -- unless it is older than delete_days.
Those two predicates are complements over this single number, so their
permitted sets are disjoint by construction and no plan can ever be in both.
Duplicating `33` into two scripts is exactly what would create the deadlock:
a 34-day-old plan with one open box would be simultaneously must-delete and
must-not-delete, and no commit would satisfy both. So neither gate may inline
the number.
THE THIRD DOOR, added by W12 (2026-09-06). The housekeeping gate no longer
demands a DELETION, because the operator's standing rule is that nothing is
deleted and a gate whose only remedy is forbidden has only one real exit: the
allowlist, which is a suppression rather than an answer. A finished plan is
now COMPACTED instead -- `worklist.py --plan-compact` replaces it with an
attested record that KEEPS ITS OWN PATH, so every citation still resolves,
while the full text moves into a content-addressed git blob that survives the
`gh pr merge --rebase` this repo merges with. A `Status: compacted` plan whose
`Full-Text-Blob:` resolves is exempt here and counted; `Status: parked` (text
compacted, work unfinished) deliberately stays on the clock. The pointer is
verified in depth by check:ci-plan-record.
WHAT THE AGE INSTRUMENT ACTUALLY IS, corrected 2026-09-06. This comment used
to assert 'AGE IS CONTENT AGE, not last commit touching the path', and that
was never true of the code: check-plan-housekeeping.sh measures
`git log -1 --format=%cI -- <path>`, and its own header explains at length WHY
last-commit is the right instrument (a plan genuinely being executed is being
edited, an edit is a commit, and a commit resets the clock -- an oracle nobody
can forge by typing a word in a Status header). The old text also claimed
archiving buys nothing because 'an archived plan's blob never changes'. That
reasoning does not hold either: a move is a commit touching the new path, and
the gate's corpus is the NON-RECURSIVE `git ls-files agent/PLAN-*.md`, so an
archived plan leaves the corpus entirely rather than ageing out in it.
Archiving therefore HIDES a plan, which is why compaction exists: a record is
still in the corpus, still at its own path, and still readable.
warn_days exists because this gate is clock-driven: its verdict can flip
overnight with no commit, which scripts/lib/suppression-liveness.ts normally
bans. The warn band is what makes that exception humane -- a plan announces
the date it will go red about a week before it does.
THE RECORD-STATUS VOCABULARY, added by W12 P3.3 (2026-09-09). `record_states`
is the set of `Status:` words that mark a plan as a COMPACTION RECORD rather
than a live plan. It is here and not inlined for one reason: the two
housekeeping twins each hard-typed the alternation `compacted\|parked` into
their own regex (`.ci/scripts/quality/check-plan-housekeeping.sh` and
`.ci/rediacc_ci/quality/plan_housekeeping.py`), and a third copy sat in
`.ci/rediacc_ci/tests/test_quality_plan_housekeeping.py`. Three copies of one
vocabulary is the `254 fast gates` shape: adding a state means finding all
three, and missing one makes a plan a record in one reader and an offender in
the other.
IT IS A MIRROR, NOT THE ORIGIN. The canonical vocabulary is
`wl_planrec.RECORD_STATES` at `.claude/hooks/stop/wl_planrec.py:155`, which
`.ci/scripts/quality/check_plan_record.py` already imports by name rather than
re-deriving. The housekeeping pair cannot import it: that gate must stay
runnable in a checkout where `.claude/` is absent, which is why it reads a
config file at all. So this key is a mirror, and the mirror is CHECKED in both
directions by test_quality_plan_housekeeping.py. A mirror nobody compares is
just a fourth copy.
